data.narrative:
Auriga Space is a Series A–stage space and aerospace company founded by Winnie Lai that has raised $12.2M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a broader comp universe of 5 public companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private peers including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs, though narrow peer matching within the same stage proved insufficient for direct comparison.

Only one triangulation method was applicable. Stage-Progression anchors to the $12.2M total raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $24M. The Peer-Median method could not be applied due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables with sufficient overlap (the sector contains 14 total peers but only 2 at adjacent stages). Public-Comp Anchoring was inapplicable because the target's revenue is not on file; while the Space & Aerospace public median trades at 27.4x P/S, this multiple cannot be deployed without disclosed revenue.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $21M to $28M, with a median point estimate of $24M. This range reflects low confidence intervals around a single method. Key uncertainties include the absence of disclosed revenue, which precludes revenue-based valuation cross-checks, and the thinness of same-stage private comparables in the sector. Additional disclosure on revenue or bookings would materially improve precision.
